items.description: 自媒体作者卡兹克分享自己搭建近一年的Agent自动化系统，核心是把任务起点从人身上移开，由事件触发Agent工作。系统分为自动化中台、Agent执行、CI中台和飞书决策四层：中台用rules.json统一管理事件触发和Agent调度，本地MacMini跑Agent任务，自建CI中台完成审查、检查、合并、发布、核实五步，只在删数据、花钱、改方向等关键决策时通过飞书卡片找作者拍板。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/dzwfvd9xp6v4qaj6olxezpier

items.description: 据彭博社10月31日报道，Alphabet、Meta、微软、亚马逊和甲骨文五大巨头承诺未来数年在数据中心等领域投入超过3万亿美元（约20.01万亿元人民币）。其中谷歌支出承诺超1万亿美元、接近一年前的八倍，Meta超8,000亿美元且近半用于最长分30年支付的租约；甲骨文是首家因投资AI数据中心而自由现金流转负的大型科技公司，预计到2028年恢复正自由现金流。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/htfc0ler37j2h4hoqll6jewz3

items.description: IT之家 11 月 2 日消息，据市场监管总局，10 月 28 日，全国网络销售重点工业产品合规提质现场活动在浙江省平湖市举办。此次活动以“学新规明准则守安全提品质”为主题，旨在宣贯《网络销售重点工业产品质量安全监督管理规定》，督促电子商务经营者增强合规意识，落实网络销售重点工业产品质量安全义务，提升网售产品质量安全水平。 公告称，加强网售工业产品质量安全治理，是守护人民群众线上消费安全的重要举措，也是推动平台经济健康发展的必然要求。活动现场对各电子商务经营者发出倡议，要守牢合规经营“硬底线”，当好质量安全“守门人”，吃透《网络销售重点工业产品质量安全监督管理规定》各项要求，加快内部质量管理制度建设，切实扛起质量安全主体责任。 IT之家注意到，活动现场， 淘天、京东、拼多多、小红书、抖音、快手、苏宁易购、唯品会、美团、腾讯 等 22 家平台企业签署了落实网络销售重点工业产品质量安全管理自律公约。北京、上海、江苏、浙江、广东等重点地区市场监管部门作交流发言。淘天、京东等电子商务平台企业及有关平台内经营者交流了产品质量安全治理经验。

U.S. data centers use 17 to 19 billion gallons of water to cool their hot-running chips each year — and that number is expected to triple in the next five years, according to The Water Foundation. That’s an expensive and politically tricky proposition for investors throwing billions of dollars at the challenge of scaling up AI. One way to use less water is to do a better job monitoring the cooling fluids, a task that currently involves sending samples away to a laboratory for tests in a multi-day process. Omen AI was founded in 2024 to solve that problem. The company is building a real-time sensor to determine whether valves were failing, or if bacteria growth in the system threatened to choke off water flow. After raising a $31 million Series A in June, Omen is now acquiring competitor Aquatic Labs in a $16 million cash-and-stock deal. The deal came together after Omen founder Zach Laberge was introduced to Aquatic Labs’ CEO Allan Adams by an investor in the filtration space. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has even suggested that it will become increasingly acceptable to meet your social and romantic needs through AI . This all led TechCrunch’s Amanda Silberling to wonder if AI executives are simply too out-of-touch to build products for normal people — a crucial question with Anthropic set to go public just as Wall Street begins losing its appetite for heavy AI spending . On the latest episode of the Equity podcast , Kirsten Korosec, Sean O’Kane, and I chatted with Amanda about why industry leaders can sometimes seem so tone deaf. Kirsten wondered if this is more of a marketing problem or a product problem.

During a recent interview with Wired’s Steven Levy , Apple CEO John Ternus defended the company’s current position in the AI landscape. Over the past couple years, Apple has often been described as behind on AI, especially as it delayed the release of a more powerful version of Siri, which finally launched this summer . But while Ternus — a longtime Apple executive who officially became CEO at the beginning of September — acknowledged that “everyone has an opinion,” he insisted, “I really like where we’re at.” Ternus added that Apple is “absolutely going to leverage AI” in its new products, but he said, “We don’t want to ship AI for AI’s sake. When we’re doing it right, people won’t have to think about whether it was AI that made this happen or more traditional software. What matters is, did we build something that they really love?” And when Levy pressed him on whether AI might affect Apple and its ecosystem more dramatically, with agents potentially making things like apps unnecessary, Ternus replied,”That could make life really easy, I suppose, but the creation of products is a deeply human and personal thing, something that we love to do.”

A federal judge denied a motion by xAI seeking to dismiss an NAACP lawsuit accusing the SpaceX-owned company of failing to obtain permits needed to operate the gas turbines powering its Colossus data center outside Memphis. Suing on behalf of the NAACP, the Southern Environmental Law Center said the AI company had “installed and operated at least 35 combustion turbines and other sources of air pollution at the Colossus site without ever obtaining the necessary preconstruction or operating air permits.” It also accused xAI of violating the Clean Air Act. xAI sought to have the lawsuit dismissed, claiming that the turbines are exempt from permitting requirements because they’re mobile. The company also argued that the plaintiffs did not have the standing to sue. “Because the plaintiffs have statutory standing under the Clean Air Act, because the combustion turbines are not ‘mobile sources’ under Mississippi’s [State Implementation Plan], and because the citizen suit provision does not violate Article II of the Constitution or the private nondelegation doctrine, the plaintiffs’ claims will proceed,” Judge Debra M. Brown wrote in her decision .
